title: Versioned availability cache for hotel bookings
name: Hotel availability cache

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code invalidates cached availability after reservations or price changes? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does invalidateHotel increment a counter instead of deleting the cached keys?
choices: DEL is not supported by ioredis for string keys
Incrementing also refreshes the TTL of every cached day
It invalidates every date for the hotel in one atomic command without knowing which date keys exist
It makes the cache write-through instead of cache-aside

questions.prompt: A get() call reads version 4, then misses and starts loading from the repo. Meanwhile a reservation commits and bumps the version to 5. The get() then writes its result. What does the next get() for that date see?
choices: It misses under version 5 and loads fresh data from the repo
It hits the entry just written and returns pre-reservation availability
It hits the entry just written, but the entry has the post-reservation data
It throws, because the version changed during the fill

questions.prompt: What is the main cost of this invalidation scheme under a hotel with heavy booking traffic?
choices: Old versioned entries are never removed and leak memory forever
Every reservation drops the cache for all dates of that hotel, lowering the hit rate and sending more reads to the repo
Each read needs a SCAN over all keys of the hotel
Reservations block until all readers finish
